idl_sources.summary: This is the routine behind iris_xcontrol -> iris_moment(fit='moment') -> iris_xmap. It sets err = sqrt(wd>0.) in DN, which the source calls a 'kluge' (:28), with no readout noise and no photon conversion. Both error computations are commented out: interr at :103, and the velocity and intensity error blocks at :113-129. So interr and velerr stay fltarr zeros (:81, :89) and are written to w[3]/w[4] as 'Ierr'/'Verr' (:141-144). Verified: iris_xmap's Ierr and Verr maps are all zeros for IRIS moments, so there are no IDL IRIS numbers to compare against.

This is the only iris_xmap path with non-zero Ierr and Verr. It runs mpfitpeak with measure_error = sqrt(wd>0) (:43, :108-109). Ierr is perr[0], the error on the Gaussian amplitude, not on the summed intensity (:113). Verr is perr[1]/refwvl*c (:115). This is a fit error, not a moment error, and belongs to wp6-m3-template-fits.

idl_sources.routine: eis_moment::moment (Hinode/EIS original the IRIS copy came from)
idl_sources.summary: This is the live version of the formula that is commented out in the IRIS copy. Missing samples get err2 = 0 (:111). Ierr^2 = sum_line sigma^2 + (nlpx/ncpx)^2 * sum_cont sigma^2 (:126, :153), which covers the continuum subtraction coherently. Ierr then gets relative gain and effective-area errors (:154) and is multiplied by the dispersion (:157). Verr = sqrt(sum_line [(lam_k - lam_c)/I * sigma_k]^2)/refwvl*c (:139-148), exactly first-order d(lam_c)/d(I_k). There is no width error.

This is the SSW per-sample sigma for IRIS: FUV gain 6, yield 1.5, dark_unc 3.1 DN; NUV 18, 1.0, 1.2 DN (:407-418). It sets x = wd_p>0 + dark_unc_p^2 and err = sqrt(x)/dn_to_p (:445-451). By IDL precedence (https://www.nv5geospatialsoftware.com/docs/Operator_Precedence.html, where > and + share a level and associate left to right) this is (wd_p>0) + rn^2, so negative DN get readout noise only (:375-376). That is the same model as irispy PR #179 and irispy's constants (utils/constants.py:22-35). The routine also flags values between -199 and -10 and 16183 DN as missing (:377-389). irispy does not.

iris_xcontrol_moments builds obj_new('iris_moment', fit=...) (iris_xcontrol.pro:484-486) and calls iris_xmap (:490). iris_moment__define.pro:134-142 dispatches 'moment', 'gauss' or 'dgf'. iris_xmap (https://sohoftp.nascom.nasa.gov/solarsoft/iris/idl/uio/ql/iris_xmap.pro) only displays w[*]. It computes no errors itself.

reports.algorithm:
Current estimator on irispy main (utils/moments.py): crop to the wings (:109-128); copy to float and set masked, non-finite and negative samples to 0 (:129-132); w_i = d_i, or d_i*dlam when integrated=True (:142-147); I = sum w; lam_c = sum lam w / I; s^2 = sum (lam - lam_c)^2 w / I; width = s (:149-158); velocity = (lam_c - lam0)/lam0*c; velocity_width = s/lam0*c (:184-196).

Proposed first-order propagation. It treats samples as independent (covariance between samples ignored) and takes per-sample sigma_i from cube.uncertainty.array, scaled by dlam when integrated=True:
1. Take one boolean `dropped` = mask | ~isfinite(d) | (d < 0), computed before zeroing. It replaces the inline condition at :132 and is applied to both d and sigma (sigma_i = 0 where dropped). sigma is cropped with the same wing slicer (:123-127).
2. sigma_I = sqrt(sum sigma_i^2).
3. sigma_lam_c = sqrt(sum (lam_i - lam_c)^2 sigma_i^2) / I. This is exactly EIS Verr before the /lam0*c.
4. sigma_{s^2} = sqrt(sum ((lam_i - lam_c)^2 - s^2)^2 sigma_i^2) / I. The d(lam_c) term drops out because sum (lam_i - lam_c) d_i = 0. Then sigma_s = sigma_{s^2} / (2 s), which is NaN where s = 0.
5. sigma_v = sigma_lam_c / lam0 * c and sigma_vwidth = sigma_s / lam0 * c. lam0 is taken as exact.
6. Apply the same intensity==0, min_intensity and saturation NaN rules (:150-176) to the error maps.

About 25 lines. No continuum term, because main has no continuum subtraction. Errors are marginal only: cov(I, lam_c) is not returned.

Clipped samples. Setting a negative sample to 0 is non-linear, and its exact derivative is 0. The recommended default is that dropped samples carry no error. Monte Carlo (scratch mc_moments.py; FUV model 4 photon/DN, 3.1 DN read noise; native 0.02596 A/px; Gaussian sigma 0.05 A; wings +/-0.3 A; 20000 realisations run through main's calculate_moments) gives the ratio of median analytic sigma to MC std for I / centroid / width:
- No negative samples (50 DN background): 0.999 / 0.997 / 0.996 at 1000 DN and 1.004 / 1.000 / 1.002 at 100 DN. The formulas are exact.
- Zero background with the drop-sigma rule, 20-43 % negative samples: 1.01-1.19 / 1.08-1.22 / 1.21-1.24.
- Zero background with the keep-sigma rule (readout-only floor from #179): 1.02-1.56 / 1.26-1.74 / 1.60-1.89.
- 2 DN background: drop 1.00-1.08 / 1.05-1.10 / 1.10-1.11; keep up to 1.31.

Both rules are conservative. Dropping is 2-4x closer to the MC. The error bars do not include the clipping bias: width comes out 1.03x the truth at 1000 DN, 1.24x at 100 DN and 2.3-2.9x at 10 DN and below, with a centroid bias of a few mA.

Interaction with calculate_uncertainty:
- On main, sigma is NaN only below -rn^2 in DN: -38.4 DN for FUV, -25.9 DN for NUV, and the -200 fill. Between that and 0 it is below the readout noise.
- Under the drop rule every negative or masked sample has sigma = 0 anyway, so the result is identical with or without PR #179. Verified on real data.
- Under the keep rule, #179 is required.

1. Exact hand check: a 3-sample spectrum with known sigma, asserting sigma_I, sigma_lam_c, sigma_s and sigma_v to rtol 1e-12.
2. Monte Carlo test with a fixed seed: Gaussian on a 50 DN background (no clipping), N about 4000. The analytic/MC ratio for all five products should be within 5 % (sampling error about 1.1 %). The scratch run gave 0.996-1.004 at N=20000.
3. Clipping-regime test: zero background, faint line. Assert analytic >= MC std, so the errors stay conservative, and document the bias.
4. Equivalence with the :148-161 test: masked, NaN and negative samples give the same errors as the clean spectrum without them.
5. Pixels removed by min_intensity, saturation or zero intensity have NaN, masked errors. A cube without uncertainty gives output identical to today's.
6. integrated=True scales sigma_I by dlam and leaves the centroid and width errors unchanged.
7. IDL cross-check: IRIS iris_xmap cannot be used (its Ierr and Verr are zeros). Instead, port eis_moment::moment :139-157 as a numpy reference (gain and aeff terms 0, no continuum pixels) and assert that Verr and Ierr*disp equal irispy's velocity_error and integrated intensity error to rtol 1e-10. Assert the per-sample sigma equals the iris_getwindata model, which #179 already matches.

reports.effort_days: 1-2 days. About 25 lines of code and one kwarg; about 6 tests, including a vectorised Monte Carlo; docstring and changelog. The main unknown is review turnaround on the API choice. Wrapping the readers in StdDevUncertainty would add about half a day as a separate PR.
risks: The error bars are statistical only. Setting negative samples to 0 biases faint lines: width 1.2x the truth at 100 DN and 2.3-2.9x at 10 DN and below, plus a centroid shift of a few mA. The errors do not cover this. The docs must say so and point to min_intensity.
Linearisation breaks down at low SNR (I/sigma_I below about 5), where the centroid and width errors become meaningless. Recommend documenting this, not masking automatically.

Level 2 spectra are resampled onto the wavelength grid, which correlates neighbouring samples. The propagation assumes independent samples, the same assumption as iris_getwindata. Lossy-compression noise is ignored.

cube.uncertainty is UnknownUncertainty from the readers, so the code must assume it holds a standard deviation (the red_blue.py:90 precedent). A user who supplies variance in a bare array gets wrong errors.
Memory: two or three extra float64 temporaries the size of the window (about 0.4 GB each for a 5e7-element window). They add to the float64 copy moments.py already makes.

The plan text 'iris_xmap's Ierr/Verr' is misleading, because IRIS iris_xmap moment errors are zeros. A glue done-when that compares against IDL numbers cannot be met. Compare against a numpy port of EIS eis_moment instead.

If glue-solar subtracts a continuum mean before calling irispy (wp2-m2-line-definition), treating the continuum error as independent per sample underestimates sigma_I. The coherent term is n_line^2 * sigma_cont_mean^2 (eis_moment :153). red_blue.py:113-117 makes the same independent approximation.
decisions_for_user: Output form. (A, recommended) Attach StdDevUncertainty to each existing map ('intensity', 'centroid', 'width', 'velocity', 'velocity_width'); the keys stay the same and it follows the NDData convention. (B) Add red_blue-style keys 'intensity_error', 'centroid_error', 'width_error', 'velocity_error', 'velocity_width_error'; this matches red_blue.py:174 in the same package. (C) Both.

Negative (clipped) samples. Drop their sigma (recommended: the exact linearisation, closest to the Monte Carlo, and independent of PR #179), or keep them at the readout-only floor (more conservative, up to about 1.9x the MC, and needs #179 merged).
Whether to activate propagation automatically whenever cube.uncertainty is present, with no new keyword (recommended; red_blue precedent), or add an opt-in keyword.
Whether to fix the readers separately so they wrap uncertainty in StdDevUncertainty (io/spectrograph.py:258, io/sji.py:255). This removes UnknownUncertainty and the INFO log for each cube.

Whether glue-solar's continuum subtraction should move into irispy later (a continuum_windows option in calculate_moments, with the coherent EIS error term), or stay in glue with the approximation documented.

reports.feature: Per-exposure orbital/thermal wavelength-drift correction for IRIS Level 2 spectra, a port of SolarSoft iris_prep_wavecorr_l2 (F167; plan wp0-irispy-requests item 1, used by wp5-m3-rest-from-measurement)

idl_sources.summary: The routine to port (P. Boerner, LMSAL; dated 2015-07-23 in the directory listing). It defines five lines at lines 38-43. For every raster step it averages the line's wavelength sub-window along the slit and fits a Gaussian (lines 98-106). It stores corr = wave0 - fitted centre and keeps a fit only if it is in range and has the right sign. corr_nuv comes from Ni I and corr_fuv from O I. It removes outliers, smooths with a 5-minute boxcar and fits a fixed-period sine plus a polynomial (lines 125-165). It returns a struct with corrs[file,step,line], chisq, times, tais, coord, corr_tai, corr_nuv and corr_fuv (note at line 217).
The model used with MPFITFUN: offset + amp*sin(freq*x + phase) + sum_i p_i * x^(i-3), where x is in seconds since the first exposure.

A copy of IDL 8.3 GAUSSFIT that passes STATUS through to CURVEFIT. The model is A0*exp(-z^2/2) + A3 + A4*x. It gets initial estimates by subtracting a constant (nterms=4) or a line (nterms=5) and taking the extremum; the sign of the extremum decides emission or absorption.

The per-image version used inside iris_prep. It fits Ni I (NUV) or O I / Fe II (FUV) in three slit chunks with MPFITPEAK and reports the OBS_VR Doppler term in pixels. It needs iris_mk_pointdb for the dispersion. It is not needed for the Level 2 port.

The routine ITN 26 documents (codes.txt:249-265). It fits Ni I only, cuts |dev| >= 0.051 Å, smooths over 5 minutes, fits a spline, sets FUV = -NUV (assumed anticorrelated) and turns NaN into 0. It also writes a JPEG and a genx file. Its header says that since the April 2014 pipeline, Level 2 has the thermal and spacecraft-velocity terms subtracted, so it measures only the residual.

idl_sources.routine: ITN 26 tutorial (usage and how to apply)
idl_sources.summary: Lines 127-190. Shows the output struct for the 2014-07-08 400-step raster. The correction is applied as new_data = interpol(data, wave + corr_nuv[i], wave), so corrected wavelength = L2 wavelength + corr. Reference figures: images/orbitvar_corr2.png and spic_wave1/2.png.

reports.algorithm:
Verified by reading the source.

1. Lines (name, wave0, fit window in Å, minimum mean DN, sign):
   - Ni I 2799.474, [2799.3, 2799.8], 5, absorption
   - Mn I 2801.902, [2801.6, 2802.4], 5, absorption
   - Fe I 2805.346, [2805.1, 2805.7], 5, absorption
   - O I 1355.60, [1355.4, 1355.9], 0.5, emission
   - Fe II 1392.82, [1392.6, 1393.1], 0.5, emission
   Each line's spectral window is found by wavelength (GETWINDX), not by window name.
2. For each file and each line, load the window. Set non-finite pixels and -200 to 0. Take the pixels inside the fit window; if fewer than 5, take 5 pixels starting at the first index. Use nterms=5 (Gaussian + linear background) if there are at least 7 pixels, else nterms=4 (constant background).
3. For each raster step, the profile is the sum along the slit of max(data, 0), divided by ny. If the profile's mean is above the minimum, fit it with SILENT_GAUSSFIT. Then corr = wave0 - centre. Keep it only if |corr| <= (wmax - wmin)/4 (0.125 Å for Ni I and O I, 0.2 Å for Mn I) and amplitude*sign > 0; otherwise NaN. The chi-square is also kept.
4. Pool all files and steps and sort them by TAI. corr_nuv starts from Ni I only and corr_fuv from O I only; the other three lines are only reported.
5. Outlier cut: drop points with corr - median > 0.08 Å (NUV) or > 0.05 Å (FUV). The cut is one-sided and NaNs end up in the 'good' set.
6. SMOOTH(/nan, /edge_truncate) with a width of floor(300 s / mean cadence); IDL adds 1 to an even width.
7. By default, fit a sine with a fixed period of 5856 s using MPFITFUN, unweighted, with free amplitude, phase and offset. Add min(floor(trange/5856), 3) polynomial terms in raw seconds. Evaluate the fit at every exposure. With /nosine it spline-interpolates the smoothed points instead; /nosmooth returns the raw per-step values.
8. To apply, use λ_corrected = λ_L2 + corr[step]. The tutorial resamples each step's spectra back onto the original grid.

Prototype (verified): a port at scratchpad/features/wavecorr/proto_wavecorr.py, using scipy curve_fit and uniform_filter1d, with a plot in wavecorr_proto.png. It reads only the needed wavelength columns from memmap and takes about 2 s for a 400-step raster.
- 20140708_114109_3824262996 (400 steps, 3.5 h): Ni I per step -0.018 to +0.019 Å. corr_nuv is a sine of amplitude 0.016 Å. O I averages -0.017 Å and corr_fuv runs from -0.020 to -0.014 Å. Ni I, Mn I and Fe I means agree within 0.0005 Å.
- 20180102 (320 steps, 49 min): Ni I within -0.006 to +0.002 Å.
- 20210429 sit-and-stare (1020 exposures): Ni I mean +0.001 Å.

The IDL code has quirks, and we must choose between parity and fixing them: the outlier cut is one-sided (lines 130-135), NaN points count as 'good', the polynomial is in raw seconds and badly conditioned, the 5856 s period is fixed, an even SMOOTH width becomes width+1, and MEDIAN's NaN handling is assumed (not checked) to ignore NaN.

The scientific payoff depends on the dataset. On 2018 and 2021 files the Ni I residual is ≲0.005 Å (about 0.5 km/s). On 20140708 it is ±0.018 Å in the NUV (about ±2 km/s) plus about 4 km/s of FUV offset. ITN 26 (codes.txt:265) says Level 2 since May 2014 already removes the thermal and spacecraft-velocity terms. Users may expect more than it delivers.

Example 02's OBS_VR recipe may be wrong in general. On 20140708 the NUV residual tracks +OBS_VR·λ/c (r=0.965, slope 0.88), so the recipe helps there. On 2018 and 2021 the residual does not track OBS_VR (slopes 0.02 and -0.14) even though OBS_VR·λ/c spans up to ±0.037 Å, so the recipe would add up to about ±4 km/s of error. This is based on 3 files and is not conclusive.

The FUV measurement is noisy where O I is weak; the 2021 sit-and-stare has many outlier fits. When the observation is shorter than one orbit (the 2018 file is 49 min), the fixed-period sine fit is poorly constrained.
memmap cubes are raw int16 and SGMeta has no window BSCALE/BZERO. The thresholds and sentinels (-200 versus -32768) must be handled, or the function must scale the data itself.

A per-step correction cannot be expressed in the current FITS-TAB WCS. Applying it means resampling, which interpolates and is memory heavy, or returning shifts only. The in-progress gWCS rewrite could change this; per the task it was not assessed.
Windows that do not reach 2799.3-2799.8 or 1355.4-1355.9 give NaN. Narrow Mg II windows or observations without O I produce no correction for that band.

idl_sources.summary: Thin Level 2 wrapper (T. Pereira, 2013). It opens iris_obj(file), sets wave = (getlam(iwin) + wave_comp)/10 in nm (line 53), and loops over NAXIS3 (raster step or time). For each step it calls iris_get_mg_features on descale_array(spec[*,*,i]) (lines 63-69). Outputs lc, bp and rp as float arrays of shape (nline, 2=[v km/s, I], nslit, nraster). The only option beyond the core is wave_comp, a wavelength offset in Angstrom. I did not read the iris_obj methods getlam and descale_array; I assume they return the L2 wavelength vector and the BSCALE/BZERO-scaled floats. The hesperia mirror copy is byte-identical (same md5).

idl_sources.routine: iris_get_mg_features.pro (core; contains peakdetect_lcl, gaussian_kernel, mg_single, mg_peaks_single)
idl_sources.summary: All the logic lives here. Rest wavelengths are vacuum Mg II k 279.63509493 nm and h 280.35297192 nm (line 371). /onlyk uses 279.644 nm instead (line 373), about 9.55 km/s off. Each spectrum is spline-upsampled to 300 points, then k3/h3 is found by extrema-count rules and a parabolic fit (mg_single, lines 76-220). Two passes follow along the slit: outliers more than 3 km/s from a 17-point Gaussian blur are dropped and refit from a spline guess (lines 406-428). A derivative-method pass then retries the remaining NaNs (lines 430-433), and k2v/k2r come from peak-count rules plus a 45-point spline refinement (mg_peaks_single, lines 223-361). Modification history ends in 2014. Byte-identical on the hesperia mirror.

idl_sources.routine: lclxtrem (IDL library routine by M. Buie, 1999 rewrite)
idl_sources.summary: Finds local extrema from sign changes of the first difference. It sorts them by decreasing |value| (also for minima) and removes weaker extrema within `width` samples (<= width). With no interior extremum it returns the global max or min, so callers always get at least one element. Docs: https://www2.boulder.swri.edu/~buie/idl/pro/lclxtrem.html and https://www.l3harrisgeospatial.com/docs/lclxtrem.html. Assumption: the copy IDL ships is this same algorithm; not verified against the IDL-distributed source.

idl_sources.routine: IDL built-ins SPLINE (tension spline), POLY_FIT, CONVOL(/EDGE_TRUNCATE)
idl_sources.summary: SPLINE is called with sigma=0 for spectra and peaks and sigma=1 (a real tension) for the along-slit line-centre guess. The docs say the default sigma is 1 and near-0 sigma behaves like a cubic spline, and they require increasing T. mg_peaks_single nevertheless passes a decreasing T (line 334). Unverified (IDL lib source not available here): sigma clamped to >= 0.001, the Cline/FITPACK scaling sigma*(n-1)/(x[-1]-x[0]), end slopes from 3-point quadratics, and order-independent evaluation. GDL's spline.pro (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnudatalanguage/gdl/master/src/pro/spline.pro) ignores sigma, so GDL is not a valid reference.
The Schmit et al. 2015 double-Gaussian-plus-wing profile model. It is unrelated to the feature finder; I list it only to rule it out.

reports.algorithm:
Verified by reading the IDL; line numbers refer to iris_get_mg_features.pro.

Inputs: spec(nwave, nslit) for one raster step, wave in nm (must be increasing), vrange (recommended [-40, 40] km/s), c = 299792.458 km/s.

1. For each line (k, h), vaxis = c*(wave - ref)/ref. Skip the line (outputs stay NaN, message printed) unless vaxis[0] <= vrange[0] and vaxis[-1] >= vrange[1] (line 394). Otherwise keep native samples with vrange[0]-3 <= v <= vrange[1]+3: about 31 pixels at 0.02546 A/px (2.73 km/s/px), about 16 when spectrally summed x2.
2. Upsample every slit spectrum onto npi = 300 evenly spaced velocities with SPLINE(sigma=0), about 0.29 km/s per point for [-40, 40], stored as float32 (line 403). All later thresholds are in upsampled points, so their km/s meaning scales with vrange.
3. mg_single(guess=0) for k3/h3, with pts_min = 15, pfit = 3, wdiff_max = 4, margin = 15 and lookahead = 10 points (about 2.9 km/s):
   - lclxtrem maxima and minima at width 10, sorted by position; extrema within 10 km/s of the edges are dropped.
   - Branch on the tag str(n_min)+str(n_max):
     - {12, 31, 32, 34, 54, 76}: take the middle minimum and halve pts_min to 7.
     - {22, 23, 33, 42, 43, 44}: take the lowest minimum between the two strongest maxima.
     - '21': take the lowest minimum if max/min of the minima exceeds 1.3, else use the derivative method.
     - n_max == 1: derivative method. n_min == 1: take that minimum. Otherwise keep the guess.
   - Parabolic path: find the minimum within ±15 (or 7) points of the guess, fit poly_fit degree 2 on ±3 points, and take lc = -c1/(2*c2) and I = c0 - c2*lc^2. Return NaN if the vertex is more than 4 points from the sampled minimum.
   - The derivative method is used only with /use_deriv. Inside ±15 km/s of the first maximum, on its higher side, excluding 15 points at each end, it takes the point of minimum |dI|.
4. Along-slit cleanup, two iterations (lines 407-428):
   - lcc = lc velocities with NaN set to 0, compared against CONVOL with a normalised Gaussian kernel (sd = 2, 17 points, /EDGE_TRUNCATE). With fewer than 17 slit pixels the kernel is [1] (no blur).
   - Pixels with |lcc - blur| > 3 km/s become NaN. If at least 3 pixels remain, a guess comes from SPLINE(good_idx, lc, all_idx, sigma=1), and every NaN pixel is recomputed with /force_guess. In that mode the derivative method applies when exactly one maximum lies more than 20 km/s from the edges.
5. Remaining NaN pixels are retried with mg_single(guess=5, /use_deriv) (lines 430-433).
6. mg_peaks_single (k2v/k2r):
   - If lc is NaN, lc = 0. Take lclxtrem maxima at width 10 within 50 km/s of lc; if there are more than 4, keep the inner 4.
   - 1 maximum: red if above lc, else blue. 2: blue and red in order. 3: the peak adjacent to lc on one side plus the strongest on the other, else the two strongest.
   - 4 maxima: if the outer separation is under 40 km/s, the inner separation over 13 km/s, and both outer peaks are more than 1.06 times their inner neighbours, take the outer pair. Else, if lc lies between the inner two or outside all four, take the inner two. Else apply the 3-peak rules.
   - Refine each peak by evaluating SPLINE(sigma=0) through ±3 points at 45 points spanning ±2 points (decreasing abscissa), and take the argmax.
7. Outputs are velocities in km/s relative to the fixed vacuum rest, and intensities in input units. Failures are NaN.

There is no on-limb flag, no quality flag and no bad-pixel handling. In my port, fill (-200) spectra yield finite junk, e.g. k3 = -0.22 km/s at I = -200, and off-limb pixels yield noise-driven finite values. There is no noise filtering of the spectra either; Pereira et al. 2013 §III.1 used Wiener filtering for low S/N.

IDL quirks a parity port must copy:
- lclxtrem ranks minima by |value|, so the higher-valued minimum wins within the width.
- When no lc is NaN, lcc[where(...)] with where = -1 clips to element 0, zeroing slit pixel 0 before blurring (line 411).
- The `ini` offset is wrong when the guess sits within 15 points of the spectral edge (line 205).
- /onlyk uses rest 279.644 nm.
- SPLINE is called with decreasing T.

4-7 working days for one developer:
- Port from the existing scratch prototype (~300 lines): about 1.5 days.
- irispy API: SpectrogramCube input, mask, fill and non-finite handling, quality flags, RasterCollection output, units and meta: about 1 day.
- Tests (synthetic plus IDL parity) and fixing parity mismatches: 1.5-2 days.
- Docs, gallery example and changelog: about 1 day.
- Review: 0.5-1 day.

Add 1-2 days for optional noise filtering or extra quality flags. Parity work is blocked until someone produces the IDL reference outputs.
risks: No IDL or GDL on this machine, and GDL's SPLINE ignores tension, so element-wise parity cannot be verified until someone with SSW IDL generates reference outputs.

IDL SPLINE internals are unverified: sigma clamp, end-slope rule, and behaviour with a decreasing T at iris_get_mg_features.pro:334. The sigma=1 along-slit guess spline can change which minimum is picked for a few pixels.

IDL quirks (the lclxtrem |value| ranking of minima, the where(-1) zeroing of slit pixel 0, the `ini` edge offset, /onlyk rest 279.644 nm = +9.55 km/s) force a choice between bit-parity and correctness. Fixing them makes outputs differ from published IDL-based work.

The algorithm is noise-fragile. In the prototype, k2 p95 errors reach 12-20 km/s at 400 peak counts, and Pereira 2013 relied on Wiener filtering that the routine lacks. Users of short-exposure data will see many outliers, as ITN26 warns.
The IDL has no bad-pixel or off-limb handling: fill-only and off-limb spectra give finite junk values. irispy must add masking or flags, which departs from IDL output there.
Thresholds are in upsampled points, so changing velocity_range silently changes their km/s meaning, and summed-x2 data (about 16 native samples) sit outside the conditions the routine was tuned for.

Performance is pure Python per pixel: about 2.5 min for a 400x1095 raster and about 4 min for 4000255147. That is acceptable, but glue must run it off the GUI thread with progress. Vectorising the branchy logic is not worth it.
Velocities are relative to uncorrected L2 wavelengths (no iris_prep_wavecorr_l2 in irispy; wp0-irispy-requests item 1), the same as the IDL default of wave_comp=0.
decisions_for_user: Parity or cleaned-up behaviour: reproduce the IDL quirks bit-for-bit (lclxtrem minima ranking, slit-pixel-0 zeroing, `ini` edge offset), fix them, or offer a switch?
/onlyk rest wavelength: copy IDL's 279.644 nm (a 9.55 km/s shift, which the ITN26 tutorial maps used) or always use vacuum k 279.63509493 nm and document the difference?

Bad-pixel and off-limb policy, where IDL has none: return NaN plus a quality flag when any masked, fill or non-finite sample falls in the used range, and add a red_blue-style min_intensity LOW_SIGNAL flag? Or keep the IDL outputs as they are?
Output layout: a RasterCollection of named 2D maps (k3_velocity, k2v_intensity, ...) plus quality, as red_blue.py does, or an IDL-shaped (line, feature, ...) array? Also the function and module name.
Whether to add optional spectral noise filtering (Pereira 2013 used a Wiener filter) or leave filtering to users.
Who can run SSW IDL to generate reference outputs, which crops to commit to irispy/data/test, and the size budget for them.
Slit-axis convention for the along-slit cleanup: require L2 layout (step/time, slit, wavelength) or take an explicit axis argument?

reports.algorithm:
Nothing needs porting. The cubes already use the SJI layout that irispy reads.

What real files contain (checked against 7 OBS downloaded or header-streamed into scratch):
- TELESCOP is always 'HINODE'.
- INSTRUME is 'SOT' or 'SOT/WB' for broadband filtergrams (both spellings occur, e.g. 20150830 vs 20151224), 'SOT/NB' for NFI magnetograms, and 'SOT-SP' for SP maps.
- TDET1 is 'SJI' and NWIN is 1.
- TDESC1 is 'Ca II H line', 'G band 4305' or 'TF Na I 5896'. For SP it is '6302A' in all 10 files of an OBS, and only BTYPE tells them apart: B_LOS, B_transverse, Continuum Intensity, Doppler Shift of 6301.5/6302.5 Line, field strength, inclination, azimuth, filling factor and total polarization.
- TWAVE1 is 0.
- BUNIT is 'DN = 64 photoelectrons' (FG), 'dimensionless ratio' (MG, BTYPE '(Stokes V / Stokes I)*4096'), 'Gauss', 'km/s', 'deg', or 'unitless number between 0 and 1'.
- Data are float32 with BSCALE 1 and NaN fill (8% of the G band frames), not -200.
- DSUN_OBS is 0.0.
- CTYPE is HPLN-TAN, HPLT-TAN, Time. CDELT1 and CDELT2 can differ (SP: 0.297 and 0.320).
- OBSID is the full 'YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_OBSID' stem, as in the AIA cutouts.
- HDU1 is the 20-column SJI aux array. XCENIX, YCENIX and PCi_jIX are filled; PZTX, SLTPX*, OBS_VRIX and OPHASEIX are 0; TIME can be negative (SOT frames before STARTOBS).
- HDU2 is the filename table, with 'A0' TFORMs that astropy cannot parse. irispy never reads it.
- SP files have one frame, so IDL wrote HDU1 as 1D with shape (20,), and DATE_OBS in SSW form ('8-Jan-2016 19:13:48.658').

How irispy main (49d705c) handles them today:
- read_files only passes files on to read_sji_lvl2 when INSTRUME is IRIS or SJI, starts with AIA, or the file is an SDO tarball (irispy/io/utils.py:192,196). reports.feature: UV burst detection: ports of SolarSoft iris_burst_check (Si IV 1402.77 spectra, threshold scaled by the time-dependent 1402.77 Å response) and iris_sji_burst_check (SJI 1400 images) into irispy. F130, plan item wp2-burst-detection.

idl_sources.summary: Si IV spectral burst finder. For each (step, y) pixel it takes the mean intensity in DN/s over bins within ±50 km/s of 1402.77 Å. A pixel is flagged when that mean is at least threshold × ybin and less than 10 × the median of the same bins (a particle-hit guard, switched off with /no_median). The default threshold is 500 DN/s × A_eff(1402.77, DATE_OBS) / A_eff(1402.77, 22-Oct-2013 21:00). Flagged pixels are grouped by 8-connectivity with region_grow /all_neigh on a zero-padded image, and single pixels are kept. Output is one struct per pixel: time, file, xpix, ypix, x, y, thresh, ybin, median, intensity, group, file_index. It prints the brightest pixel per group.

SJI 1400 burst finder. It finds the file with iris_find_file(date, sji=1400), which assumes a local archive layout, and reads it with read_iris_l2. For each frame it takes the median and standard deviation of the pixels that are not -200 and flags pixels ≥ median + 10σ. Groups use 8-connectivity with region_grow; isolated single pixels are dropped. Output is an IDL list with one struct per frame that has bursts: index (flat), group, int, npix, im_index, nevents, nx, ny. It uses no response or exposure scaling and no temporal linking. The header documents a sig_factor option, but it is not in the PRO signature, and line 100 hard-codes 10.

Data extraction called by iris_burst_check with (file, 1402.77, /normalize, /keep_sat). It finds the window by wavelength and sets values between -200 and -10 to missing -200 (l.378). /keep_sat keeps the 16183 DN saturated pixels (l.386). /normalize divides each step by its exposure time (l.550). wd.int is ordered [lambda, x, y], and scale[1] is the y pixel scale. time_ccsds is the shutter-open time ti1 (l.465), while irispy's time coordinate is the exposure midpoint.

Effective areas. With an undefined version it loads the newest geny and writes r.version back into the version variable (l.132). As a result, both calls in iris_burst_check use the same version, currently v009 = iris_sra_c_20231106.geny (l.112), which is the newest file in https://sohoftp.nascom.nasa.gov/solarsoft/iris/response/. iris_burst_check takes area_sg[imin,0] (FUV) at the grid point nearest 140.277 nm. For v9+, the Si IV band is flattened to its mean (l.175).
v = dλ/λ × 2.99792458e5 km/s (non-relativistic).

/ALL_NEIGHBORS gives 8-neighbour growth. The docs say 'the grown region will not include pixels at the edges of the input array', which is why the spectral routine pads the image and the SJI routine does not. Without /EVEN, MEDIAN of an even count returns the upper middle value (https://www.nv5geospatialsoftware.com/docs/MEDIAN.html).

idl_sources.routine: Young's usage page for iris_burst_check (reference output)
idl_sources.summary: Worked example on the Tian et al. (2016) dataset of 2-May-2015 02:34 (OBSID 3820109196). It lists 5 events (time, x-index, y-index, intensity in DN/s, npix) and a threshold of 465.1 DN/s. The SJI routine's header gives its own example: 22-Oct-2013 21:00, frame 0, npix 798, nevents 25, 1393×1093 image.

reports.algorithm:
SPECTRAL (iris_burst_check), per raster file or repeat:
1. Load the window containing 1402.77 Å. Values ≤ -10 DN become missing; saturated pixels are kept; each step is divided by its FUV exposure time, giving DN/s.
2. v = c·(λ − 1402.77)/1402.77. Keep bins with −50 ≤ v ≤ 50 km/s: 18 bins at 2× spectral summing, 37 at 1× (measured on local files).
3. I = mean over those bins ignoring missing values. M = median over the same bins (IDL median does not skip the -200 values).
4. Threshold T = 500 DN/s × A(1402.77 Å, DATE_OBS of the first file) / A(1402.77 Å, 2013-10-22T21:00), using the same response version for both, currently v9. A user-supplied threshold skips this scaling. ybin = round(y pixel scale / 0.166) = SUMSPAT.
5. Flag pixels with I ≥ T·ybin and I < 10·M (factor 1e10 with /no_median).
6. Label flagged pixels by 8-connectivity in the (step, y) plane. Singletons are kept. For sit-and-stare data, step is time, so groups link in time. Group numbers continue across files and are stored in a byte array, so they wrap after 255.
7. Output is one row per flagged pixel.
Spectral binning is not scaled. The IDL comment at l.154-156 says it does not need to be, but a mean per bin doubles with 2× summing, so the effective threshold is halved for SUMSPTRF=2 data. I verified this by reading the code, not by running IDL.

SJI (iris_sji_burst_check), per frame of SJI 1400:
1. From the pixels that are not -200, take the median (IDL upper median) and the sample standard deviation.
2. Flag pixels ≥ median + 10σ. This value is hard-coded; sig_factor cannot be set.
3. Label by 8-connectivity and drop 1-pixel groups. region_grow ignores array-edge pixels here because there is no padding, and a bright edge seed could loop forever. That comes from the IDL docs, not from a run. group_num is a byte and wraps at 256.
4. Output is one entry per frame with ≥1 event.
Neither routine has a size, lifetime or temporal-persistence criterion beyond these steps.

3-5 working days:
- about 1 day to port both functions (about 150-200 lines on top of existing helpers, including SpectrogramCubeSequence/RasterCollection input, window lookup by wavelength, units and output objects)

The main cost is the API and output shape plus validation, not the numerics.
risks: Exact equality with published IDL numbers is not possible on today's archive: the L2 files were reprocessed in 2026, and Young's 2017 numbers used response v4. Matching needs a fresh IDL run on the same files, or a tolerance-based comparison of event positions.

The result depends on the response version. v4 gives 465.1 DN/s and v9 gives 434.1 DN/s for the same dataset. irispy only exposes v9, and its response code is IDL-validated at a single date (2025-08-05). The ratio also uses the 2013-10-22 value, which has not been checked against IDL. The v4 match suggests it is right.

IDL quirks: the mean per bin is not scaled by spectral summing, so the effective threshold halves for SUMSPTRF=2; the median includes -200 values; the SJI routine ignores edge pixels and can loop on edge seeds; byte-typed group numbers wrap at 255/256; sig_factor is documented but cannot be set. Copying the quirks exactly or fixing them changes results on binned data.
irispy flips V34 rasters (STEPS_AV < -0.01) along the step axis, so step indices won't match IDL xpix for those observations.
irispy masks only -200. IDL also treats -200 < x ≤ -10 as missing, which changes means and medians slightly unless the port does the same.
memmap=True cubes are unscaled (raw counts) and carry no mask, so the functions must refuse them or they will give nonsense thresholds.

Science scope: these are Young's quick-look detectors, not a community-standard catalogue. The review (Young et al. 2018 SSRv, Sec. 2) explicitly recommends dataset-specific thresholds (for example k≈7σ for 1400 Å) and no fixed threshold. On active-region SJI data the 10σ rule flags every frame. The docstrings must say what the method is.
Large sit-and-stare windows (e.g. 262×417×1600) need only the ±50 km/s slice. A naive full-window float64 load uses about 1 GB.
decisions_for_user: Copy the IDL quirks exactly or fix them. The main case is scaling the threshold by spectral summing; the others are the median ignoring missing values and dropping byte wrap-around. Suggested: match IDL by default and document the binning issue, with no extra keyword unless someone asks.
Response version. Suggested: use get_latest_response (v9), which matches current IDL behaviour, and do not add a version argument to reproduce 2017 numbers.

Output types. Suggested: an integer label cube (0 = no burst) with the source's WCS, as a SpectrogramCube map for spectra and an NDCube/SJICube-shaped array for SJI, plus an astropy QTable of events: frame/step, group, npix, peak intensity, peak pixel, time, Tx/Ty. The IDL per-pixel structs and lists would not be reproduced. glue needs the label cube.
Should sigma_factor and min_pixels be real SJI parameters (defaults 10 and 2), given that IDL hard-codes them?
Should the spectral routine group across raster repeats in time? IDL groups within each file only, with global numbering. Suggested: keep IDL behaviour.
Is it acceptable to add a remote_data test that downloads the 309 MB Tian 2016 raster, or should this validation be a one-off with synthetic tests in CI?
Is anyone with IDL/SSW available to produce reference .sav outputs of both routines on current L2 files (Tian 2016 plus 4000255147)?

On current upstream main, calculate_uncertainty clips photons at 0, so sigma is finite for every finite sample, including the -200 fill. Two consequences. The 'keep' rule is no longer blocked. And 'the drop rule is independent of #179' is no longer a reason to prefer it. The implementation must also drop samples through the explicit mask and never rely on NaN sigma, which the report's `dropped` mask already does.

No independent reference exists for any of the five errors, and there is none at all for the width error. Separately, EIS Verr multiplies by raw err (:143), not err2, so a missing sample with err = -100 enters Verr as 1e4 times the weight squared. A literal port would reproduce that quirk.

'sigma_s ... is NaN where s = 0' is imprecise. With the drop rule, zero-valued (not negative) samples keep a readout-only sigma, so sigma_{s^2} > 0 and dividing by 2s gives +inf, not NaN. It is NaN only when every other sample was dropped. With option A the mask comes from the values (make_map_cube mask_invalid, _spectral.py:17), so inf or NaN errors on finite widths stay unmasked.

The per-sample model overestimates the single-sample variance: observed/predicted is 0.58 (C II) and 0.66 (Si IV). For sums over 5 and 15 samples the ratio rises to 0.75/0.85 (C II) and 0.89/0.98 (Si IV), so sigma_I from independent samples is about right to slightly conservative. corrections: Wrong: 'reads only the needed wavelength columns from memmap' and filename input being 'cheaper: reads only about 20 wavelength columns'. The rows along the wavelength axis are 1074 bytes and the pages are 16 KB, so any column slice pages in the whole window. I measured this on 20140708 Mg II k (400x1095x537 int16, 470 MB): h[8].data[:,:,250:270] touches about 540 MB of pages for a 17.5 MB slice. Reading through irispy memmap cubes or through filenames costs the same I/O, so that argument for the Input decision falls away.

The prototype does not match IDL, even though the report calls it verified. In proto_wavecorr.py:102-103, `good` is computed after the outliers were already set to NaN, so it is always all True. The outlier steps, which SMOOTH /NAN then fills, stay in the sine fit, while IDL leaves them out through the WHERE complement (iris_prep_wavecorr_l2.pro:130-135). The prototype also drops NaN before fitting, where IDL keeps them, and it tests swidth against nt, not nngood. I re-ran it with an IDL-like mask: the difference is ≤0.0001 Å on the three files, so the numbers stand but the code is not a faithful port.
iris_prep_wavecorr.pro is 183 lines, not 200. I downloaded it from the cited URL (HTTP 200) and it is byte-identical to the prototype's copy.

The report says MEDIAN's NaN handling is 'assumed (not checked)'. It is documented: 'The MEDIAN function treats NaN values as missing data' (https://www.nv5geospatialsoftware.com/docs/median.html). There is a parity difference it did not list: without /EVEN, an even-length MEDIAN returns the upper-middle value, not the average that np.nanmedian gives.

Risk 4 infers from the 20140708 residual tracking +OBS_VR·λ/c (r=0.965) that the OBS_VR recipe 'helps there'. The aux table has a POFFXNUV column, the pipeline's per-exposure spectral shift in pixels (aux header col 44). On 20140708 the Ni I residual correlates with POFFXNUV·0.02546 Å at r=-0.969, slope -0.38, and POFFXNUV itself correlates with OBS_VR (r=-0.94; -0.91 and -0.97 on the 2018 and 2021 files). A likely reading, which is an assumption, is that the pipeline over-corrected its own orbital shift by about 38%. That would make the OBS_VR match coincidental and suggest the recipe double-corrects on all three files.
The ITN 26 tutorial entry 'lines: 130' is meaningless. tutorials.txt has 361 lines; the cited range 127-190 is correct.
missing: The IDL routine assigns the wrong times on negative-step (V34) rasters. iris_data::getvar defaults to revnegdx=1 and reverses the step order of the data when PZTX decreases (https://sohoftp.nascom.nasa.gov/solarsoft/iris/idl/uio/objects/iris_data__define.pro:492-527, getdx at 1353-1361). ti2utc/gettime (1468-1485) returns times in exposure order, and iris_prep_wavecorr_l2.pro:82-83,106,115 pairs the flipped data with unflipped times. The local V34 OBS 3400109360 (STEPS_AV -0.998, PZTX 30.88→29.88→28.88) is affected. A faithful port must not copy this, and an IDL parity test cannot use V34 data. irispy flips data and times together (io/spectrograph.py:161,213,252), so the port is fine if it takes irispy objects.

IDL can return a silently wrong correction. NaN steps stay in the 'good' set; if any survive SMOOTH /NAN (the whole Ni I or O I series NaN, or a gap longer than 5 min), MPFIT's first fnorm is non-finite. It then jumps to FAIL_OVERFLOW and returns the starting parameters, and /quiet hides the error (https://sohoftp.nascom.nasa.gov/solarsoft/gen/idl_libs/astron/markwardt/mpfit.pro:3083,3236-3237,3593-3610,3697). corr_nuv then becomes 0.1+0.01·sin(...), about 0.1 Å or 11 km/s, plus 1·t+0.1·t²... when the span is at least one orbit. I read this from the source but did not run it. The port needs an explicit 'no correction' result (NaN or an exception), which is an API decision the report does not list.

This fails on real local data. In the V34 limb OBS 3400109360 (XCEN -939", YCEN 383"), the Ni I window's slit-mean is 1.2-4.8 DN, below the 5 DN threshold. The prototype gets 0/64 fits for Ni I, Mn I and Fe I and 30/64 noisy O I fits (sd 0.076 Å). The report's applicability risk covers only windows that do not reach the lines. It does not cover limb or off-limb targets, which are common IRIS science, or flares, where Mg II triplet emission at 2798.8 Å sits next to the 2799.3-2799.8 Ni I window (that part is an assumption).

The report does not mention the aux columns POFFXNUV/POFFXFUV (per-exposure spectral shift, px), POFFF* (source flag) or IT14S-IT19S (spectrograph temperatures 'for wavelength'). They show what Level 2 already corrected, bear directly on the example 02 / OBS_VR decision, and irispy does not expose them as meta. Adding them next to 'observer radial velocity' is a cheap first step.

The apply step has to handle sentinels. With memmap=True, irispy builds no mask (io/spectrograph.py:254-256) and the data are raw int16, so resampling would smear -32768 into neighbouring pixels. Sentinels must be set to NaN or masked before interpolating, and the mask and uncertainty must be shifted too.

Parity details: IDL CURVEFIT defaults to ITMAX=20 and TOL=1e-3 and returns parameters even when it has not converged, and the routine never checks STATUS. scipy curve_fit raises instead. The set of NaN steps will therefore differ, so a parity test needs a tolerance and must compare masks.

There is a possible parity route without an IDL licence. A sibling scratch directory (features/gdl-reference) has a GDL app and partial SSW gen and iris trees. It lacks silent_gaussfit.pro, and running GDL was denied here, so I did not check that it works.

Spectral summing is not covered. With NUV summing of 4 or 8 the 0.5 Å Ni I window holds 5 pixels or fewer, and IDL forces 5 pixels with nterms=4 (lines 89-90). The synthetic tests should measure precision at summing 1, 2, 4 and 8. The 2018 file is already SUMSPTRN=2.

Sequencing with gWCS is not raised as a decision. The measurement function does not touch the WCS; the apply/resample function does, and may need rework or become expressible in the WCS once the gWCS reader lands. Shipping the measurement first and the apply step later is a real option.

Scope and value decision: F167 is 'could' priority. On 2018-2021 files the NUV residual is ≲0.005 Å, and ITN 26 codes.txt:265 says Level 2 is already corrected. A measurement-only deliverable (per-step table plus recommended curve, no apply) takes about 2-3 days and should be offered as an option.

Absolute frame: the correction forces Ni I 2799.474 and O I 1355.60 to their laboratory wavelengths, so the lines' own convective or intrinsic shifts are absorbed into it. The documentation and glue's velocity caveat should say that velocities are relative to that frame (assumption, standard ITN 26 §5.1 practice).

corrections: The where(-1) quirk is described wrongly, and the prototype copies the error. The report says that at iris_get_mg_features.pro:411 `lcc[where(~finite(lcc))] = 0.0` 'clips to element 0'. WHERE returns the scalar -1 when nothing matches (https://www.nv5geospatialsoftware.com/docs/WHERE.html). From IDL 8.0 on, a scalar -1 subscript means the LAST element; in IDL 7.1 and earlier it raises an out-of-range error (https://www.nv5geospatialsoftware.com/Support/Maintenance-Detail/idl-version-80-or-greater-negative-array-indices-and-the-where-function). So IDL zeroes the last slit pixel, not pixel 0. mg_features_proto.py:236 (`lcc[bad if bad.any() else 0]`) gets this wrong. On full real slits the quirk never fires, because there is always a NaN: I patched the prototype and 12 step/line runs on 3824262996 showed 0 changed pixels. It does fire on small clean crops and synthetic tests, which is exactly what the report plans to use for parity.

The report calls SPLINE's behaviour with a decreasing T 'unverified', and its prototype evaluates the spline independently of point order. That is not what IDL does. IDL's lib spline.pro (the 2003 CT/RSI version with /DOUBLE, copyright 1983-2010 ITT VIS; copy at github.com/leonf88/envi-spectrum lib/spline.pro, and the same loop in the 1983 version at github.com/callumenator/idl external/ICUR/icur/spline.pro) finds each interval with a monotonic pointer: `for i=1L,nm1 do while tt[j] lt xx[i] do subs[j]=i ...`. With the decreasing nvel built at iris_get_mg_features.pro:334/349, every one of the 45 points is therefore evaluated on the LAST interval [vel[idg+2], vel[idg+3]]. The cubic is extrapolated about four upsampled points back; it is not interpolated. I ported spline.pro line by line (scratch idl_spline.py) and confirmed subs == [6] for every point. On 3824262996 steps 160/180/200/220 (about 4180 finite peaks per feature), IDL-faithful and prototype k2v/k2r/h2v/h2r differ by more than 1e-3 km/s in 90-93% of pixels: median 0.07-0.10 km/s, p95 0.52-0.57 km/s, max 1.1 km/s. Peak intensities differ by more than 1e-4 (relative) in 76-80% of pixels, by up to 24%. The proposed parity criterion (99% of pixels within 1e-3 km/s) would therefore fail for all k2/h2 maps. This is a second, large parity-versus-correctness choice that the report lists only as an unverified detail.

The synthetic accuracy numbers in the validation section (k2v/k2r median 0.008-0.009 km/s, p95 about 0.02, noiseless) describe the corrected algorithm, not the IDL one. With IDL-faithful refinement, noiseless k2v/k2r come out at median 0.015/0.026 km/s and p95 0.045/0.077 km/s (scratch synth_idl.py).

The other unverified SPLINE details can now be settled. The sigma clamp (`sigmaIn > 0.001`), the scaling sigma*(n-1)/(x[n-1]-x[0]) and the 3-point quadratic end slopes are all confirmed. Precision is double only if X, Y or T is double. The upsampling call (line 403) and the peak-refinement call (line 339) are therefore double, but the along-slit guess call (line 419: long, float, findgen) runs in single precision, whereas the prototype uses float64. With increasing T, the prototype tension_spline agrees with the ported IDL spline to 3.8e-6 on about 400-DN values.

missing: The IDL Level 2 wrapper double-descales data from rasters that step in the negative direction. iris_data::getvar (https://sohoftp.nascom.nasa.gov/solarsoft/iris/idl/uio/objects/iris_data__define.pro, lines 492-523; md5 matches GitHub ITA-Solar/IRIS-Software-UIO objects/) defaults to revnegdx=1. When getdx(0) < 0 it forces load=1 and returns data that are already descaled, as float, in reversed step order. iris_get_mg_features_lev2.pro:64 then applies descale_array again (I*0.25+7992). Local 3400109360 has a PZTX step of -0.998. For such rasters the SSW output is wrong: intensities are affine-shifted, and the '21' max/min>1.3 test and the |value| ranking of minima change which branch is taken. IDL reference outputs must therefore be produced by calling the core routine on explicitly descaled spectra, never the lev2 wrapper, and anyone comparing with published IDL maps needs to know about this. (Verified by reading the code, not by running it.)

memmap=True cubes are more than unmasked: they hold raw int16 values, (I-7992)/0.25, so almost everything is strongly negative. That reverses the |value| ranking of minima in lclxtrem and breaks the '21' ratio test, so every pixel changes, not only the fill pixels. The port must rescale or reject unscaled cubes (io/spectrograph.py:156 uses do_not_scale_image_data=memmap). Otherwise the whole map is silently wrong.

If the port reuses red_blue._prepare_data (red_blue.py:88: `data < 0 -> NaN`), a single negative sample turns the whole spline, and so the whole pixel, into NaN, which departs from IDL. This belongs in the bad-pixel policy decision.

The 279.644 nm /onlyk rest may be intentional. Line 372 shows the vacuum value commented out and replaced, possibly as an empirical offset for early L2 wavelengths. Treat it as 'intent unknown, ask the author (T. Pereira, UiO)', not as a bug.

A new decision the report does not list: copy IDL's extrapolated peak refinement, which is equivalent to a biased k2 estimator, or evaluate correctly. The choice changes k2/h2 values by up to about 1 km/s and intensities by up to 24%, so it matters more than the other quirks listed.

The parity plan should ask the person running IDL to dump intermediates (spc, lc after each cleanup pass, lclxtrem outputs), not only the final lc/bp/rp. The branch logic is chaotic and the along-slit cleanup couples 17 neighbours, so without intermediate dumps every mismatch costs another round trip to someone with IDL.

Reuse and provenance: ITA-Solar/helita (BSD-3, same group) has a Python lclxtrem/peakdetect_lcl in helita/utils/utilsmath.py:372-421. It is not usable as-is: it uses np.bool and its no-extremum path returns a boolean mask. It is still worth citing and asking about, because the IDL looks like a port of Python code that might exist unpublished. The upstream MIT licence of the UiO code is compatible with irispy; the report does not mention licensing.

verdicts.reasoning:
The report is mostly right. It reads the algorithm correctly: I re-fetched the sources from sohoftp, hesperia and the ITA-Solar GitHub, and all three are identical. Its irispy file:line citations check out except cosmic_rays.py:71, and the data headers are correct. But it is wrong or unverified on exactly the points that decide whether IDL parity is achievable, and those points drive the effort.

1. The where(-1) quirk zeroes the LAST slit pixel in IDL 8 and raises an error in IDL 7.1. The report and prototype zero pixel 0.

2. More important: IDL's SPLINE (checked against a copy of the IDL 8.0 lib source and ported line by line) finds intervals with a monotonic pointer. With the decreasing T at lines 334/349, all 45 refinement points are evaluated on the last interval, so the peak refinement is an extrapolation. On real 3824262996 spectra this moves k2/h2 by median 0.1 km/s, p95 0.5 km/s and max 1.1 km/s, and intensities by up to 24%, in more than 90% of pixels. The proposed 1e-3 km/s parity criterion would fail everywhere unless this is copied, and the report's synthetic accuracy figures describe a corrected algorithm, not the IDL one.

3. The report missed two input traps:
- SSW's lev2 wrapper double-descales data from negative-step rasters, and local 3400109360 is one.
- irispy memmap=True cubes are raw negative int16, which reverses lclxtrem's minima ranking. Only fill values were considered.

Each of these adds a decision (parity versus correct, and which IDL entry point produces the references), a fixture or test, and probably extra round trips to someone with IDL. The prototype makes the numerics cheap, so coding plus the irispy API plus docs is about a week. Parity work with an external IDL holder, the new quirks and chaotic branch sensitivity push a validated port to about 7-12 days (L). The report's M is achievable only if parity is dropped in favour of a documented 'IDL-derived, corrected' implementation.

I agree that a short decision record is needed before coding. It must now also cover: extrapolated versus correct peak refinement; generating references by calling iris_get_mg_features on explicit descaled spectra with intermediate dumps; scaled-data and negative-value policy; and asking the original author whether the /onlyk 279.644 nm rest was intentional.

corrections: The report says 3893012099 'has only Si IV 1394, so it is a good refusal case'. That is wrong. Its window is named 'Si IV 1394' but spans 1380.7-1406.7 Å (primary header TWMIN/TWMAX), so it contains 1402.77. IDL iris_data::getwindx (https://sohoftp.nascom.nasa.gov/solarsoft/iris/idl/uio/objects/iris_data__define.pro l.614-623) picks the first window whose wavelength range contains the input, and iris_getwindata calls it for any input > 1000 (l.271). The report's own meta.spectral_range lookup would select it too. I ran it: 37 bins, T = 86.5 DN/s, 0 px, no refusal. The irispy sample raster 3683602040 is the same case: its only Si IV window is 'Si IV 1394' covering 1380.7-1406.7 Å. The glue done-criterion 'refuse other windows, e.g. 3893012099' is therefore invalid, and window lookup must go by wavelength coverage, not by TDESC name.

The report says 'the effective threshold is halved for SUMSPTRF=2 data'. The framing is wrong. I streamed the L2 header of Young's reference dataset for the 500 DN/s threshold (22-Oct-2013 20:59, OBSID 3820259443, https://iris.aws.lmsal.com/data/level2_compressed/2013/10/22/20131022_205938_3820259443/iris_l2_20131022_205938_3820259443_raster.tar.gz): SUMSPTRF=2, SUMSPAT=1. The Tian example is also SUMSPTRF=2. So 500 DN/s is calibrated on 2x-summed data. The quirk makes the threshold effectively 2x too high for SUMSPTRF=1 data (4000005156, 3893012099) and 2x too low for SUMSPTRF=4 data (3602506433, sample 3683602040). A 'fix' must scale by SUMSPTRF/2, not by SUMSPTRF, or it breaks the Young/Tian reproduction. Checked on 3602506433: the IDL rule flags 4 px in 1 group at 86.5 DN/s, and the max mean is 143.9 DN/s, so a SUMSPTRF/2-normalised threshold of 173 DN/s flags nothing.

The report says the prototype was 'run against an irispy main export' and shows 'both algorithms fit in about 60 lines'. In fact bursts/proto.py reads raw FITS sections with astropy and uses irispy only for get_latest_response. None of the irispy object path was exercised: read_spectrograph_lvl2 → SpectrogramCube with FITS-TAB WCS, masks, V34 flip, sunraster apply_exposure_time_correction, and read_sji_lvl2 → SJICube with gWCS. The 60 lines are the numerics only, not the port.

The report says irispy test data allow 'smoke tests only' because the files are 'trimmed'. They are more limited than that. The Si IV 1403 test windows (20140329 r000xx, 8x109x29; 20210905, 187x40x29) are rebinned about 10x in wavelength (29 bins over 1398.6-1405.75 Å) and have only 2 bins within ±50 km/s. They cannot exercise the averaging or the median guard, so synthetic fixtures need a hand-built WCS and SGMeta.

The v4 465.1 DN/s check could not use 'irispy's response code with the v4 geny' directly: get_latest_response has no file argument, and ratio_tian.py monkey-patched ROOTDIR. irispy also applies the v9 Si IV flattening unconditionally (irispy/utils/response.py l.135-147). The report says a grep for 'burst' finds only test overview.txt files. On origin/main 49d705c, git grep -i burst finds nothing at all. The overview.txt hits came from installed irispy 0.8.1 (features.json F130). This does not change the conclusion that there is no burst code.

Verified as stated: the IDL line citations (burst_check l.121-137, 143, 154-156, 162-168, 180-195; sji l.2, 69, 100, 115-130; getwindata l.378, 386, 465, 550-561; get_response l.132, 112, 175-184); both reference headers (Young's page table and 465.1 DN/s; the SJI doc example 798 px, 25 events, 1393x1093); Young et al. 2018 SSRv Sect. 2 recommending dataset-specific thresholds with k≈7 for 1400 Å; the REGION_GROW edge and -1 wording; the Tian result reproduced by an IDL-faithful re-implementation (upper median including -200, same 32 px / 6 groups, identical to the nanmedian version); and 4000255147 (4 px, 1 group, T = 627.2) and SJI 1705 events.

verdicts.reasoning:
The numerics are small and I confirmed them. I re-downloaded both IDL routines, iris_getwindata, iris_get_response, lamb2v, SSW average.pro and iris_data__define.pro, and checked the cited lines. I rewrote the spectral detector IDL-faithfully (upper median including -200, missing handling as in IDL) and got the same 32 px / 6 groups on the Tian 2015 raster: Young's 5 events at the same positions, plus one extra singleton. The report is also optimistic about the port. Its prototype bypasses irispy's readers, WCS and objects. The test data cannot exercise the ±50 km/s logic. The gallery sample data give 0 spectral bursts and flag every SJI frame. And zero-exposure steps and SJI memmap handling are not covered.

No separate plan is needed, but before coding the user should answer four quick questions in the irispy issue: normalise to SUMSPTRF/2 or copy IDL, the label cube dtype and shape (which fixes the glue interface), which dataset the gallery uses, and whether to add a remote-data test. Whether this is wanted at all is still open, since F130 is only 'could' priority.

corrections: SPLINE claim is wrong. The report says a clamped-end SPLINE variant changed Mg lc/rp/bp by exactly 0, so the shim's end conditions do not matter. That variant (gdl-reference/harness_clamped/spline.pro) used 2-point end slopes and still ignored tension, so it modelled neither thing that makes IDL's SPLINE different. IDL's SPLINE sets sigma = sigma > .001 and uses 3-point quadratic end slopes (IDL spline.pro copy at https://github.com/callumenator/idl/blob/master/external/ICUR/icur/spline.pro; SSW gen/idl/genutil/dspline.pro has the same clamp). So spline(...,0.) at iris_get_mg_features.pro:339/354/403 is a near-cubic spline with different end slopes, and :419 is a real sigma=1 tension spline. GDL's own spline.pro is idlastro's natural cspline with no sigma argument. I re-ran drv_mg under GDL with a double-precision port of IDL's algorithm (verify-gdl-reference/h_sorted_dbl, run_sorted_dbl, cmp_mg.py). Against the report's natural-spline shim: 35 k3 and 17 h3 line centres flip between finite and NaN (of 6216 each); 1-2% of lc/rp/bp values move by more than 0.1 km/s, up to 25-47 km/s, driven by the sigma=1 call alone (run_sig1_dbl); and about 8% of h peaks and k blue peaks move by more than 0.1 km/s (p95 0.17-0.37 km/s).

A second SPLINE problem is missed. iris_get_mg_features.pro:334 and :349 build nvel in decreasing order (from vel[hlim] down to vel[llim]). IDL documents T as 'must be strictly increasing' (https://www.nv5geospatialsoftware.com/docs/SPLINE.html). The IDL spline.pro copy finds intervals with a forward while-loop that puts decreasing T in the wrong interval, and SSW's dspline.pro sorts T before calling SPLINE for exactly this reason. With that loop (run_loop_dbl), 53-58% of rp/bp velocities differ from the shim by more than 0.1 km/s, and the medians shift by 0.08-0.23 km/s. Whether current IDL still behaves this way is unknown without IDL. So the Mg-features GDL reference is not a validated IDL stand-in, even as a working assumption.

CURVEFIT description is wrong. GDL's curvefit.pro is not a clean-room gradient-expansion fitter. It is a wrapper that calls SSW's gen/idl/fitting/mpfit/mpcurvefit.pro (listed in run_deps/deps_sorted.txt) with ftol=tol left undefined, so MPFIT's defaults apply (ftol 1e-10, up to 200 iterations). IDL's CURVEFIT uses gradient expansion with TOL=1e-3 (relative chi-square decrease) and ITMAX=20 (https://www.nv5geospatialsoftware.com/docs/CURVEFIT.html). silent_gaussfit.pro:282 passes neither, so the defaults are what run. I passed IDL's defaults through to mpcurvefit (h_cftol/curvefit.pro) and re-ran drv_wavecorr: per-step corrs moved by up to 1.1e-3 Å (Ni I), 2.0e-3 Å (Fe I) and 1.65e-2 Å (O I), and corr_fuv moved by up to 0.015 Å on a total range of 0.094 Å. The proposed 'rtol about 1e-5 for fits' is therefore not achievable against IDL, and saying agreement is 'assumed' understates a sensitivity I measured. CHISQ also means something different: mpcurvefit returns the unreduced weighted sum of squared residuals (mpcurvefit.pro:223).

'No stable macOS GDL build' is wrong. MacPorts has gnudatalanguage 1.1.3 (https://ports.macports.org/port/gnudatalanguage/). Confirmed as stated: conda-forge has neither 'gdl' nor 'gnudatalanguage' (micromamba search), and Homebrew's 'gdl' is the GNOME Docking Library. Also, the weekly-release tag is overwritten every week (current assets published 2026-09-22), so the exact macOS build used (1.1.2-55-g7e299bbc) cannot be downloaded again. That contradicts presenting it as a regeneration path.

Provenance is weaker than claimed. ssw_manifest_md5.txt has 179 entries, all .pro files, with no iris/response .geny files. iris_get_response.pro:116-117 picks the last iris_sra_c_* file by file_search plus last_nelem, so a new response version in SSW would silently change the burst threshold (iris_burst_check.pro:129-136), and the md5 manifest would not catch it.

The float32 argument does not support the conclusion drawn from it. IDL's TOTAL sums float input in single precision and uses the thread pool (TPOOL_* keywords; https://www.nv5geospatialsoftware.com/docs/TOTAL.html). SSW stdev.pro is two TOTAL calls on float data. Each SJI 1400 image is 388x417 = 161,796 pixels, which I believe (from memory, not checked) is above IDL's default TPOOL_MIN_ELTS of 100000. If so, IDL's boundary pixels depend on the thread count, and 'a float32 sequential sum gives 237, like GDL' does not predict IDL's answer. Even an IDL certification run would vary by machine at the threshold.

irispy_today misses existing infrastructure and a licence problem. irispy/conftest.py:73-75 already pulls larger fixtures with pooch from https://github.com/LM-SAL/irispy-lmsal-test-data, which is the natural home for full-sampling crops and .sav references. irispy/data/test ships in the wheel (pyproject.toml:90, include-package-data = true), and the harness's strmatch.pro is a modified copy of a GDL file whose header says 'part of GDL - GNU Data Language (GPL)'. Putting the harness at irispy/data/test/idl/ as proposed would ship GPL code in a BSD-2-Clause package (licenses/LICENSE.rst).

The 4-file wavecorr run on 3602506433 has 32 steps (4 files x 8), with 20 usable O I fits against a sine plus polynomial model; it is a smoke test, not a reference.

missing: The main decision is missing: what should the ports match? The options are (a) IDL's numerical artefacts: CURVEFIT stopping early (TOL 1e-3, ITMAX 20), the sigma=1 tension spline, and possibly the undefined behaviour of SPLINE with decreasing T; or (b) mathematically converged answers. scipy-based ports will naturally agree with GDL/MPFIT, not with IDL. This choice decides whether a GDL reference is useful at all for Mg features and wavecorr.

Before GDL outputs are labelled IDL references, the SPLINE shim has to become a faithful Cline tension spline (sigma > .001, 3-point end slopes, double precision when X or T is double), and CURVEFIT needs a shim that emulates gradient expansion with TOL 1e-3 and ITMAX 20. The alternative is to restrict the IDL-reference claim to the two burst checks, which avoid both routines.

The IDL certification run should target the known divergences directly: SPLINE with decreasing T and sigma 0 or 1, CURVEFIT iteration count and converged parameters, and TOTAL/STDEV on float arrays over 100k elements. It should also check whether REGION_GROW returns -1 for an edge seed and whether TEMPORARY errors on an undefined argument. A plain end-to-end diff would not pin down the causes.

Tolerances should be absolute and in physical units (for example Å for corrs and corr_nuv/fuv, km/s for Mg features, and a count of allowed pixel flips for masks), not rtol. Relative tolerance is meaningless for corrections near zero; I saw relative differences up to 3.4x for O I.

iris_sji_burst_check starts group_num at 1b and adds 1b per group, so with more than 255 groups in one image, labels wrap to 0 and those pixels drop out of where(group GE 1). A port has to reproduce or document this, and the fixtures should say whether any image comes close.
Pin the response file: record the md5 of iris/response/iris_sra_c_*.geny, or pass version= in the drivers. Also pin the apt package version in the Ubuntu Docker recipe.

verdicts.reasoning:
The prototype works as described. I checked the scratch harness, the line counts, all the SSW URLs (they return 200, and one is md5-identical to the local copy), the irispy file:line citations and the data headers. The report's weak point is the step from 'runs under GDL' to 'a usable IDL parity reference'.

Two of the four routines depend on library code where GDL clearly behaves differently from IDL:
- **Mg features (SPLINE):** replacing the natural-spline shim with IDL's tension-spline algorithm changed 1-2% of values by tens of km/s, flipped 35 k3 and 17 h3 line centres between finite and NaN, and moved about 8% of peaks by more than 0.1 km/s. The IRIS code also calls SPLINE with decreasing T at lines 334 and 349, which IDL does not support; modelling IDL's interval-search loop moves more than half of the peaks by over 0.1 km/s.
- **Wavecorr (CURVEFIT):** GDL's CURVEFIT is MPFIT with an ftol of 1e-10, while IDL stops at TOL 1e-3 after at most 20 iterations. Using IDL's stopping rule alone moved O I fits by up to 0.016 Å and corr_fuv by up to 0.015 Å, which rules out the proposed rtol of 1e-5.

The report's own sensitivity check could not show either effect, because its clamped variant ignored tension and used the wrong end slopes.

The report is also wrong that there is no stable macOS GDL (MacPorts has 1.1.3). The weekly macOS build it used cannot be downloaded again, the md5 manifest leaves out the response file that sets the burst threshold, and placing the harness under irispy/data/test would ship a GPL file in the BSD wheel. It also missed the existing pooch test-data repo.

The burst-check references hold up best: they rely only on a REGION_GROW shim and on float32 median/stdev, and thresholds flip at boundaries in IDL too.

A plan is needed first, and it is more than the half-day the report suggests. It has to settle what the ports should match (IDL's quirks or converged answers), make the shims faithful or narrow the IDL-reference claim to the burst checks, and define the IDL certification run around the specific divergences. The effort estimate is therefore optimistic: 5-8 days for the full job, or M if scoped to the burst checks.

Side effect to disclose: before I saw that gdl.app/Contents/MacOS/gdl is a launcher that runs 'open -a Terminal', I ran it three times. Up to three Terminal windows with idle interactive GDL sessions may have opened on the user's machine and can be closed. All real runs used Contents/Resources/bin/gdl.

Evidence files are in <scratch>/features/verify-gdl-reference/: cmp_mg.py, icur_spline.pro, the h_* harness variants (spline.pro/spline_core.pro, h_cftol/curvefit.pro) and run_*/out/*.sav.
